clue.text: One-time network's extracts helping to make rubber

indicators.note: 'One-time' read literally says the word keeps only one of its two Ts, so a T is dropped

parts.note: a lattice is a network of crossing strips; the 's makes it plural here

explanation.surface: Some once-used network supplies the extracts from which rubber is made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-time' looks like 'former', but it tells you LATTICES must have only one T: drop the second to leave the plural of latex.
explanation.definitionFit: Latex, the milky sap of rubber trees, forms its plural with -ices, and these saps are the raw material of natural rubber.

clue.text: OT character going around as an ornamental tree

indicators.note: the Old Testament figure's name goes around the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Lot is a figure in the Old Testament (OT), Abraham's nephew
qua is Latin for 'in the capacity of', i.e. as

explanation.surface: Some Old Testament figure wanders about posing as a decorative tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The loquat is an evergreen fruit tree from East Asia, widely planted for decoration.

clue.text: Unproven explanation of the Circle Line?

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
RY is an abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone wants a speculative account of London's Circle Line underground route.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle Line is a London Underground route; here 'Circle' is O and 'Line' a railway, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation that has not yet been proved.

clue.text: See 11
Dismisses antipodean type?

indicators.note: the antipodes lie upside down from Britain, so in a down clue the word is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.surface: An Australian or New Zealand sort of person sends people packing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Antipodean type' suggests an Aussie character; 'type' is the definition in its printing sense, with the question mark flagging that a serif is part of a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a letter in many typefaces, so it is a feature of printing type.

clue.text: Hippy cup-bearer's after brother with a force before lunch

indicators.note: the cup-bearer is placed after the earlier pieces

parts.note: dint means force, as in 'by dint of'
Hebe was cup-bearer to the gods in Greek myth; the 's is 'is'
a.m. is the morning, the time before lunch

explanation.surface: A broad-minded hippy serves drinks with a forceful sibling ahead of the midday meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hippy' is not a flower child but someone wide in the hips.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wide across the hips and buttocks is described idiomatically as broad in the beam, from a ship's width.

clue.text: I'm surprised outlaw's eaten rat

indicators.note: 'outlaw's eaten' means the outlaw has swallowed the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a bandit is an outlaw; the 's stands for 'has'
coo is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation as the outlaw turns out to have devoured a rat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandicoot is the name of a large South Asian rat as well as an Australian marsupial.

clue.text: Tributary to furious European river

indicators.note: the words feed a short stretch of letters into the answer, which flows out of them

explanation.surface: A side stream feeds a raging continental river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tributary' seems to be the definition, but it signals the letters lying across 'furious European'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is a name shared by several English rivers, notably in Yorkshire and East Anglia.

clue.text: Having restricted view, say, one in road snarled up M1 north of Coventry

indicators.note: traffic snarled up is tangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the 1 is read as the letter I

indicators.note: in a down clue, the northernmost part of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A motorist complains of poor visibility on a jammed M1 above the city of Coventry.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is England's main north-south motorway. 'snarled up' jumbles I and ROAD into DIORA; M1 gives MI; 'north of Coventry' gives its top letter, C.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama shows a scene seen through a small window or opening, so it offers a restricted view.

clue.text: It's said Mnemosyne's daughters stun Mercury and others who had limited influence in the past?

definitions.text: who had limited influence in the past?

indicators.note: the sound of the spoken words is what counts, not their spelling

parts.note: Mnemosyne bore Zeus nine Muses, so her daughters are nine; stun means daze
Freddie Mercury fronted the rock band Queen with three others

explanation.surface: The Muses dazzle a rock singer and his band, who once wielded little power.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Jane Grey held the English throne for only nine days in 1553, hence her limited influence.
explanation.definitionFit: Lady Jane Grey, England's briefest monarch, reigned so short a time that her power was slight.

clue.text: See 8
Evidence in book of ducks' feathers signals the end of the show

definitions.text: signals the end of the show

parts.note: in a cricket scorebook a batter out for no runs, a duck, is recorded as 0, a ring
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: Evidence of waterfowl in a bird book: their plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's duck is a score of nought, written as a circle in the scorebook, hence rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre rings down the curtain when a performance finishes, so the phrase marks the close of a show.

clue.text: Wind caught by misdirected craft? For certain I'll be responsible

definitions.text: Wind caught by misdirected craft? For certain I'll be responsible

parts.words: Wind caught by misdirected craft? For certain I'll be responsible
parts.note: a person who guides aircraft through the sky would take the blame for a plane sent astray

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the person in the control tower answerable for every aircraft's course.
explanation.definitionFit: The official who directs aircraft movements is the one held accountable when a plane goes off course.

clue.text: Call from lookout to get off a boat

parts.note: to land is to disembark, getting off a vessel
a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel

explanation.surface: The lookout shouts that it is time to disembark.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors on watch traditionally shout this cry when they first sight a coast.

clue.text: See 22
Imps left in depression by citation in New York

indicators.note: the last piece stands beside the rest

parts.note: a col is a dip between mountain peaks

indicators.note: the citation sits inside the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Mischievous creatures abandoned in a hollow, cited in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: LINCOLN CITY is an English football club nicknamed the Imps, after the Lincoln Imp carving in its cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Imps is the nickname of the football club based in Lincoln, England.

clue.text: Fresh coinage of some lingo

indicators.note: fresh means new, a sign these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A newly invented term taken from a bit of jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly invented word or expression is called a neologism, from Greek for new word.

clue.text: Hand-held tools staggered this loony

indicators.note: loony means crazy, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A madman reels about with tools in his hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Rulers for drawing true lines are tools held in the hand.

clue.text: Invalid only replaces love in Milton's heart

indicators.note: one word stands in for another, here in the middle of the name

parts.note: Milton Obote was a president of Uganda
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
sole means only

explanation.surface: A disabled person: the poet Milton's sole love lies in his heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Milton looks like the poet, but it is Milton Obote of Uganda: 'in Milton's heart' points at the middle O of his surname, which SOLE replaces.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obsolete is out of date and no longer valid.

clue.text: For starters, romantics want a bottle of fizz here?

definitions.text: For starters, romantics want a bottle of fizz here?

parts.words: For starters, romantics want a bottle of fizz here?
parts.note: a restaurant setting laid for a courting couple sharing champagne before the first course

explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' is both 'to begin with' and the first course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant reservation for a couple is where a romantic dinner with champagne would happen.

clue.text: Way bits of groping react advantageously?

definitions.text: Way bits of groping react advantageously?

parts.note: via means by way of

indicators.note: the opening bit of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A route by which fumbling advances get a favourable response.
explanation.definitionFit: The impotence drug promises that clumsy advances meet a favourable physical response.

clue.text: She, indeed, has modelled

parts.note: aye means yes, indeed

indicators.note: modelled means shaped anew, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Indeed, she has posed as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She' is not a pronoun but Rider Haggard's novel She, whose title character is Ayesha.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayesha is the immortal queen known as She-who-must-be-obeyed in H. Rider Haggard's novel.

clue.text: See 12
Unitary connection involving us either side of single item of newsflash?

definitions.text: Unitary connection involving us either side of single item of newsflash?

indicators.note: involve once meant entangle or roll up, so all these letters are tangled together
just one letter, the first, is taken from the word

explanation.surface: A link between units wraps us around a breaking news headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single item of newsflash' is its first letter, N, with US placed either side of it; since everything is then mixed by 'involving', the placement only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcasters who link programmes together between items of news provide the joining thread of a channel.

clue.text: It's to be respected and spymaster bears the burden

parts.note: to tote is to carry a load
M is the spy chief in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A thing worthy of reverence, with a spy chief shouldering the load.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a revered emblem, an object treated with great respect by a clan.

clue.text: Island cooler after drug drop?

indicators.note: the letter ends up after the rest
the drug letter drops, moving down to the foot of the word

parts.note: an Esky is an Australian brand of portable cool box
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An island cooled after someone dropped a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Esky is the Australian name for a picnic cool box; move its E to the end. Skye is a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the largest island of the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland.

clue.text: What's presented by the treacherous SOB carrying weight condition

indicators.note: the outer word carries the others inside it

parts.note: greet is Scots for weep or sob
kg, kilogram, is a unit of weight
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: A traitor's offering: a sobbing wretch weighed down with conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: SOB looks like an insult in capitals, but it is the verb, Scots GREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek gift is a present given to deceive, after the Trojan horse.

clue.text: See 16
See 5
Some slap mum, who bears single result of injury

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a scar is the mark left by a wound
a means one, single

explanation.surface: Mum, who carries a scar from a blow, gets hit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slap' looks like a blow, but it is slang for make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Slap is theatrical slang for make-up, and mascara is one kind of it.
